en: Could you give me more information, please?
note: Information → información shows -tion → -ción. Me da... por favor is a courteous request.
Reservation → reservación. Reserva is another common word for a booking.
Invitation → invitación. These -ción nouns are feminine: la invitación.
Situation → situación. Keep the written accent on the final syllable.
Solution → solución. Hay means there is or there are.

en: Could you give me an explanation, please?
note: Explanation → explicación shows -tion → -ción. Da is the usted present form of dar.
Option → opción. Buena agrees with feminine opción.
Connection → conexión is an exception to a simple -tion → -ción swap.
Communication → comunicación. Spanish often uses an article for a general concept.
Conversation → conversación. Fue presents the conversation as a completed event.

en: I would like your authorization, please.
note: Authorization → autorización shows -tion → -ción. Quisiera and su make the request courteous.
Celebration → celebración. Hoy can naturally go at the start of the sentence.
Decision → decisión: many -sion nouns have Spanish -sión cognates.
Confusion → confusión. Algo de expresses an unspecified amount.

en: I feel a lot of pressure.
note: Pressure → presión shows that similar Spanish endings do not always come from English -sion.
Impression → impresión. English -ssion often corresponds to Spanish -sión.
Version → versión. Tu versión is the subject of gusta.
Conclusion → conclusión. Esa agrees with the feminine noun conclusión.
Expression → expresión. English double s becomes a single s here.
Television → televisión. Vemos is the nosotros form of ver.
Opportunity → oportunidad: a useful -ty/-dad cognate pattern.
Responsibility → responsabilidad. Many -ity words correspond to -idad words.
Quality → calidad. The spelling of the stem changes; endings alone are not enough.
Activity → actividad. The -ity/-idad pattern appears in many common nouns.
University → universidad. These -dad nouns are usually feminine.
Reality → realidad. Esa refers to the feminine noun realidad.
Possibility → posibilidad. English -bility often corresponds to -bilidad.
Honesty → honestidad. This noun follows a useful pattern rather than a letter-for-letter swap.
Basic → básico/básica. The adjective agrees with feminine pregunta.
Public → público. Many -ic cognates end in -ico and carry a written accent.
Fantastic → fantástico. Suena is the él/ella form of sonar.
Historic → histórico. The adjective normally follows momento here.
Logic/logical → lógico. A Spanish -ico adjective can match English -ic or -ical.
Typical → típico. Día is masculine despite ending in -a.
Automatic → automático/automática. Puerta requires the feminine form.
Technical → técnico/técnica. Ayuda is feminine, so use técnica.
Delicious → delicioso/deliciosa. Comida requires the feminine ending.
Famous → famoso. Some English -ous adjectives correspond to Spanish -oso.
Generous → generoso. Use generosa when describing a woman.
Nervous → nervioso/nerviosa. Está describes how she feels today.
Curious → curioso. Here curioso means unusual or interesting.
Mysterious → misterioso. The stem changes spelling as well as the ending.
Clearly → claramente shows -ly → -mente. Podría makes a polite request.
Normally → normalmente. Normal has the same form for masculine and feminine.
Perfectly → perfectamente. Perfecta + mente makes an adverb.
Easily → fácilmente. Fácil keeps its written accent when -mente is added.
Finally → finalmente. Final + mente forms the adverb.
Simply → simplemente. Sé is the yo form of saber and has a written accent.
Really → realmente. English -ly often corresponds to -mente, but not in every word.
Constantly → constantemente. Constante + mente forms the adverb.
